props.title: Halloween
props.initialSlug: Silent killer stalks babysitters on Halloween night

sections.content: Halloween revolutionized slasher films with John Carpenter's masterful direction and minimalist terror. The film's genius lies in its restraint - Michael Myers stalks through suburban shadows while Carpenter's piercing piano theme creates unbearable tension. This launched Jamie Lee Curtis's career as the original "final girl" Laurie Strode and established crucial slasher conventions: the unstoppable killer, teenage victims, and holiday setting. Black Christmas (1974) laid some groundwork, but Halloween perfected the formula that Friday the 13th (1980) and A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984) would soon follow.

movies.title: Halloween
movies.slug: John Carpenter's seminal slasher follows masked killer Michael Myers terrorizing babysitters on Halloween night. Defined the genre with its iconic score and methodical suspense.

movies.title: Black Christmas
movies.slug: Proto-slasher about sorority sisters stalked by an unseen killer during Christmas break. Influenced Halloween's POV shots and holiday horror.

movies.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
movies.slug: Raw, visceral horror about teens encountering a family of cannibals. Like Halloween, it suggested more violence than it showed.

sections.content: Carpenter's visual style in Halloween proved enormously influential. He used wide Panavision shots to hide Myers in plain sight and pioneered the killer's POV through that legendary opening sequence. The film's success sparked the 1980s slasher boom, with Prom Night (1980), My Bloody Valentine (1981), and countless others copying its template. But few matched Halloween's craftmanship - Carpenter built scares through composition and timing rather than gore. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Impact

Halloween's DNA appears in countless modern horror films. Scream (1996) directly referenced its tropes while subverting them. It Follows (2014) borrowed its relentless walking killer and suburban dread. You're Next (2011) and The Babadook (2014) updated the "final girl" concept for new audiences. Even Get Out (2017) used Halloween's technique of making daylight scenes unsettling. The 2018 direct sequel Halloween proved the original's staying power by bringing back Curtis and treating Myers as a grounded threat rather than supernatural being.
